newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico data spur fresh look at Q2 GDP forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Mexico data spur fresh look at Q2 GDP forecasts.

text.p: Economists on Thursday were busily revising their estimates of Mexico's second-quarter economic growth after industrial production data released earlier in the day blew most forecasts out of the water.

A stronger-than-expected 9.9 percent rise in June industrial production -- and an 11.2 percent gain for the quarter -- triggered yet another rally by Mexican stocks, after the monthly figure left the consensus forecast of an 8.3 percent increase looking pale.
"This is a very clear piece of data telling us that Mexico is growing at a faster pace," said Lucia Domville, Latin America economist at Santander Investment.
"Now that the elections are over and Mexico has shown itself to be a stable market, people will definitely be revising their GDP forecasts upwards," Domville said.
The industrial production report is the last major economic reading before second-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) is announced next Tuesday.
Industrial production accounts for about 25 percent of GDP, while services represent about 63 percent and mining and agriculture about six percent, one analyst said.

Before the industrial production report, a Reuters survey of 13 Mexico City economists showed an average second-quarter GDP forecast of 5.92 percent, though most say that figure appears to be too conservative in view of the fresh data.
Many economists are now looking for growth to come in somewhere between the earlier consensus and 7.0 percent.

The industrial production increase indicates "very high GDP growth ... knowing that the service sector has started to recover and its recovery is accelerating," said Rogelio Ramirez de la O, director of independent economic advisors Ecanal.

Arguing that GDP rarely comes in more than four percentage points below the industrial production figure, he has been forecasting second-quarter GDP growth as high as 7.0 percent for the past two weeks, making him one of the most bullish.
He has revised his year-end GDP forecast to 6.0 percent, against an official forecast of 4.5 percent, in part because of Thursday's industrial production data.

J.P. Morgan economist Alfredo Thorne, who forecast second-quarter industrial production at 11.8 percent, is sticking to his robust second-quarter GDP estimate of 6.6 percent and is looking for 5.4 percent increase for the year.
"Services could bring a surprise," he said, adding reviving consumption could boost that GDP component.

Rodrigo Brand, Mexico economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said the firm was maintaining its forecast of 5.7 percent GDP growth for the second quarter, though he added the increase may come closer to 6.1 percent.
For the full year, he is looking for 4.8 percent growth, with a view to revising that estimate to about 5.0 or 5.1 percent.

Santander Investment, which raised its second-quarter GDP estimate two weeks ago to 5.5 percent, has no plans to revise that forecast. Still, Domville said the number could well come in on Tuesday at about 5.8 or 5.9 percent.
